display.title: The Alter Rebbe Frees the Chassan, Part 1
display.summary_short: Why the builders of the Tower of Bavel were spared, and how a town's joyful wedding for two orphans turns to sorrow when a cruel official arrests the chassan.
display.summary_long: After the song, the storyteller introduces a story about the Alter Rebbe's Ahavas Yisroel: love every Jew and look for the good in him. From Parshas Noach he asks why the generation of the Flood was destroyed while the builders of the Tower, whose sin was worse, were only scattered, and answers with Rashi: they had achdus. In the story, the Alter Rebbe arranges a match between two orphans, and the whole town joyfully shares the work of the l'chaim, the wedding and the new home, except for Moshe, the richest man in town, who never gives more than a nickel, so no one asks him. On the wedding morning the town's Jew-hating official, who fines Jews for any excuse, arrests the chassan and announces he will be drafted into the army for 25 years, threatening the community leaders with Siberia. The town turns to Tehillim, and at noon the Alter Rebbe's wagon pulls up at the shul. The storyteller adds that the Rebbe taught that looking at a tzaddik's picture brings encouragement and connection. To be continued.
display.lesson: Love every Jew, see the good in others and include everyone; achdus protects the Jewish people.
